details: Escalating geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran have triggered a "risk-off" sentiment across global financial markets, significantly impacting cryptocurrencies. On September 1-2, 2026, renewed U.S. military strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz, followed by Iranian retaliation, led to a sharp decline in Bitcoin and other digital assets. Bitcoin's price fell below $77,000, reaching lows around $76,762, and over $100 million in leveraged long cryptocurrency positions were liquidated within an hour. This downturn mirrored broader market movements, with the S&P 500 also declining and U.S. Treasury yields rising. Concurrently, oil prices surged, with Brent crude climbing above $94 a barrel, intensifying concerns about inflation and potential disruptions to global energy supplies. The market reaction underscores how geopolitical instability can lead investors to reduce exposure to volatile assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: US-Iran Tensions Escalate, Bitcoin Tumbles Below $77,000
